question:
(a) Describe the motion of free electrons in a conductor before and after applying an electric field.
(b) Explain why current is established almost instantly in a conductor even though the drift speed of electrons is very small.

options.A:
(a) Electrons are stationary before an electric field and move at the speed of light after it is applied.
(b) Current is instant because drift speed is very large.
options.B:
(a) Random thermal motion itself produces current before applying the field; after applying it, electrons move in the direction of the field.
(b) Current takes a long time to be established.
options.C:
(a) Before applying the field, free electrons have random thermal motion with zero average velocity; after applying it, they acquire small average drift velocity opposite to the field.
(b) Frequent collisions keep drift speed small, but the electric field is established throughout the conductor almost immediately, so electrons begin drifting nearly simultaneously.
options.D:
(a) Free electrons move only in one direction before the field is applied.
(b) Current is instant because collisions stop completely.
